newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris to light millennium countdown clock.
newsitem.headline: Paris to light millennium countdown clock.

text.p: France starts its countdown to the next millennium on Saturday night when Paris Mayor Jean Tiberi lights a clock on the Eiffel Tower which will click down the 1,000 days to the year 2000.
Tiberi will throw the switch to illuminate the clock and the entire tower about four minutes before 12 a.m. (2200 GMT) to allow time for its lights to reach full brightness by midnight.
At the stroke of 12, a dozen fireworks rockets will rise into the sky before exploding in colourful sparks, a spokeswoman for Paris city hall said.
The ceremony will be the highest-profile event so far in France's preparations to celebrate the new millennium.
Several French cities will organise large festivals over the next three years and an advertising campaign was launched on Thursday under the slogan: "1,000 days to create the year 2000."

The national committee organising the celebrations will randomly select 20,000 French people who will mark their 20th birthday in the year 2000 for all-expenses-paid trips to destinations around the world.
